whyCandidate: Seven roles run from a Tata Steel traineeship through cement-plant E&I leadership to site delivery of a food plant. The record includes an electrical supervisor licence, NEBOSH, SAP PM, and quantified availability and breakdown results. It is hands-on industrial electrical work, not data-center operations.
whyJob: Cloudflare's data center operations engineer racks, cables, replaces hardware, and troubleshoots servers and network gear on site. The physical work is real, but the equipment and the employer are a cloud network, not a cement kiln or a 132 kV substation.
success: Lead with plant availability, breakdown reduction, commissioning, and the electrical supervisor licence. Describe troubleshooting and maintenance planning in the candidate's own plants. Do not claim data-center racking, server repair, or Cloudflare product experience.
failureModes: Rewriting cement-plant commissioning as data-center build-out
Dropping the electrical licence because the posting does not name it
Inventing server, Linux, or network-gear troubleshooting
whyItMatters: Skilled industrial engineers are often screened out of infrastructure jobs, or padded into them. A useful product has to show the transferable maintenance record without changing the industry.

whyCandidate: The same long industrial record includes SAP PM/PS, spares inventory, work instructions, and maintenance plans. Most of the seven roles are site electrical work that a DCIM administrator would not perform.
whyJob: The DCIM administrator owns Nlyte work orders and the record of every physical change on Cloudflare's network. Accuracy of asset records matters. Nlyte, Move/Add/Change control, and a global cloud network are not in the resume.
success: Emphasize SAP PM, spares inventory, work instructions, and maintenance plans. Leave kiln, wagon-loader, and extrusion-line detail off or in a short earlier-career section. Do not claim Nlyte or data-center inventory administration.
failureModes: Keeping all seven roles at equal length
Translating SAP PM into Nlyte
Burying the inventory and work-instruction evidence under project values
whyItMatters: Long industrial resumes fail when every project stays on the page. They also fail when a familiar system name is swapped for the posting's tool.

whyCandidate: The candidate leads electrical installation and holds an electrical supervisor licence, PLC exposure, and SAP PM. Nothing in the record is Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible, or software reliability.
whyJob: GitLab's staff site reliability role designs multi-tenant environment automation with Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes. The seniority and the tools are both beyond the resume.
success: Refuse the staff SRE framing. A truthful resume stays an electrical and instrumentation record. It must not add infrastructure-as-code, Kubernetes, or staff software leadership. The electrical licence must not be presented as a cloud credential.
failureModes: Mapping PLCs to Kubernetes
Promoting plant leadership to staff SRE
Treating the electrical supervisor licence as a cloud certification
whyItMatters: A stretch posting is where a tailoring product is most tempted to invent a career. Licensing language makes that invention dangerous.

whyCandidate: The record is an Army logistics career: a 2,260-person special operations supply chain, freight across road, sea, and air, SAP, and a parachute sustainment company. The dataset domain label says legal. The jobs do not.
whyJob: Cloudflare's logistics operations specialist coordinates delivery of data-center hardware, reverse logistics, and spare parts with vendors. The function matches. The commodity is servers and racks, not military freight.
success: Lead with distribution, vendors, inventory, and the SAP-backed freight operation. Keep ranks and unit names accurate. Do not recast special-operations logistics as data-center hardware deployment the resume does not describe.
failureModes: Calling the candidate a lawyer because the dataset domain is legal
Replacing GATES and ICODES with unnamed data-center systems
Dropping the scale figures that make the logistics record specific
whyItMatters: Military logistics is a common civilian transition. The product should translate the function without erasing the service or inventing the new industry.

whyCandidate: The candidate has directed logistics programs and purchasing, at O-4 and as a company logistics manager. The record does not mention server manufacturing, L10 builds, or rack integration.
whyJob: The supply-chain program manager connects capacity demand to L10 server supply and L11 rack integration. The posting calls the role a senior individual contributor in hardware supply planning.
success: Show program leadership, purchasing, and multi-party freight. State the hardware-manufacturing gap by omission: do not claim L10 or L11 planning. Do not inflate an O-4 logistics command into manufacturing-supply seniority the posting defines differently.
failureModes: Inventing rack-integration experience from the word logistics
Copying L10 and L11 into the resume
Dropping the only quantified supply results
whyItMatters: Adjacent supply-chain titles are where keyword overlap hides a different kind of supply planning.

whyCandidate: Compliance work is ITAR/EAR on logistics, plus a Top Secret clearance in the published record. There is no network security, firewall, DDoS, or customer-support engineering.
whyJob: Cloudflare's network security engineer supports customers on Magic Transit, DDoS, network firewall, and the web application firewall. The word security appears. The work is product support, not military logistics.
success: Do not convert ITAR compliance or a clearance into network-security engineering. A truthful result either keeps the logistics identity or declines the match. Clearance may be stated only as published, not as a security-engineering qualification.
failureModes: Treating ITAR as network security experience
Adding Cloudflare product names
Using the clearance to imply a security career
whyItMatters: Clearance and compliance language is a known way resumes get rewritten into security jobs the person has not done.

whyCandidate: The candidate is a Pega lead business architect for a US state health-agency client, with earlier banking product analysis. The degree is mechanical. The health work is systems delivery for an agency, not clinical care.
whyJob: Datadog's senior business systems analyst owns internal business functions, discovery, and delivery, and the posting says it is not a generalist BSA role. It also expects agentic tools and MCP. Pega and a health-agency client are not those systems.
success: Lead with intake, audit trails, Direct Capture workshops, and backlog ownership. Keep the health-agency client as a systems client. Do not claim clinical practice, MCP, or Datadog product development.
failureModes: Turning a health-agency implementation into healthcare practice
Adding MCP or AI-agent delivery
Ignoring the posting's warning that a generalist BSA is the wrong shape
whyItMatters: Agency and healthcare-adjacent systems work gets misread as clinical qualification, and a familiar BA title gets over-claimed against a posting that rejects generalists.

whyCandidate: The candidate facilitates Pega workshops and writes backlog narratives for banks and a health agency. The resume has no marketing campaigns, advertising ROI, or dashboard analysis.
whyJob: Elastic's fixed-term marketing analyst uses existing dashboards to explain campaign performance and ROI. The shared word is analyst. The subject is regional marketing.
success: Do not recast Pega workshops as marketing analytics. A truthful resume keeps business-analysis and rules-engine work and does not add campaign ROI.
failureModes: Equating any analysis with marketing BI
Inventing dashboard or ROI claims
Hiding the Pega specialty to sound like a marketing hire
whyItMatters: Title overlap is enough to produce a confident, wrong career story. An applicant who has never worked in marketing would then be holding a resume that claims they had.

whyCandidate: The candidate leads Pega discovery and scrum. The education line is mechanical engineering. No bullet describes application code, compilers, or security research.
whyJob: GitLab's backend role extends program analysis, call graphs, taint analysis, and SAST rules. It is a software engineering job that shares the word security with many postings and nothing specific with this resume.
success: Do not present Pega configuration or workshop facilitation as backend engineering or static analysis. The mechanical degree must not become a software degree.
failureModes: Calling business-rules work software engineering
Adding SAST, CWE, or OWASP experience
Changing the degree
whyItMatters: This is the career-change failure the product has to refuse: a strong analyst pressed into a developer identity.

profession: Education IT support and LMS lead
whyCandidate: The strongest evidence is Canvas and LMS administration at a police academy and two colleges, plus faculty training. Several bullets are only 'Monitor staff progress' or 'Handled office, student services, and admin processes.' Earlier roles are academic secretary.
whyJob: Datadog's learning technology specialist provides tier 2 and tier 3 LMS support, vendor incidents, upgrades, and documentation. That is the work the detailed bullets already describe, written weakly.
success: Lead with Canvas administration, faculty training, and the academy LMS role. A rewrite may clarify those duties only within the words already present. Do not invent ticket volumes, and do not drop the secretary roles if they are the only early chronology, but do not let them lead.
failureModes: Leaving 'Monitor staff progress' as the lead line
Inventing a number of tickets or learners
Promoting an online teaching certificate into instructional design the bullets do not show
whyItMatters: Real LMS résumés are often vague. The product should make the real platform work easier to see without inventing scale.

profession: Education IT support and LMS lead
whyCandidate: The candidate has campus IT support, CCNA, web administration, and an ERP training bullet. The support is for colleges and a corporate Drupal site, not a global edge network.
whyJob: Cloudflare's technical support engineer helps customers with application performance and developer-platform products and wants internet-technology depth. Support experience transfers. The products do not.
success: Show help-desk and site-administration support, CCNA, and ERP training as support evidence. Do not claim Cloudflare products, DNS expertise, or developer-platform support that the resume does not contain.
failureModes: Filling the resume with internet-protocol keywords from the posting
Dropping Canvas because the posting is not about education
Treating CCNA as Cloudflare network engineering
whyItMatters: Support candidates get keyword-stuffed toward the employer's product stack. The resume then reads as product experience the person cannot defend in an interview.

profession: Education IT support and LMS lead
whyCandidate: The ceiling of the record is LMS administration, campus IT support, and CCNA. Secretary work is part of the early record. There is no infrastructure-as-code or staff engineering role.
whyJob: The GitLab staff SRE role requires Terraform, Ansible, and Kubernetes at staff scope. CCNA and server-side Canvas hosting are the only nearby facts, and they are not that job.
success: Keep the candidate at campus IT and LMS scope. Do not invent staff SRE work from CCNA or from hosting Canvas on a firm server.
failureModes: Expanding CCNA into Kubernetes
Treating Canvas hosting as multi-tenant SRE
Erasing the secretary chronology to look more senior
whyItMatters: A certificate plus the word server is enough for a model to award a staff title.
includeEvidence: Canvas hosted on a firm server

whyCandidate: Four security roles include incident response, UEBA, playbooks, a GCIH certification, and specific reduction figures for vulnerabilities, MTTR, and staff incidents. The writing is already quantified and slightly promotional.
whyJob: Twilio's incident-response engineer leads response, writes runbooks, and works across threat activity. That is the center of the resume, not a stretch.
success: Lead with IR playbooks, the contained intrusion, MTTR, and GCIH. Keep the percentages attached to the role that stated them. Do not add Twilio-specific systems or a staff title.
failureModes: Repeating the same MTTR story across employers
Dropping GCIH
Smoothing a specific breach into a generic security achievement
whyItMatters: A strong security resume tests whether the product can order real evidence instead of only repairing weak bullets.

whyCandidate: SSO appears once, as help delivering SSO at Transurban. The rest of the career is detection, IR, firewalls, and program leadership. IAM design is not the job history.
whyJob: Cloudflare's IAM engineer designs workforce and workload identity, SSO with SAML, OIDC, OAuth, and SCIM, and an identity governance platform. SSO is the overlap. Protocol design is not in the resume.
success: Mention the SSO delivery as limited, attributed evidence. Keep IR and detection as the career. Do not claim SAML, OIDC, SCIM, or identity-governance ownership.
failureModes: Expanding one SSO bullet into an IAM career
Adding protocol names from the posting
Dropping IR because the posting is about identity
whyItMatters: One overlapping bullet is how adjacent security specialties get over-claimed. A single SSO delivery becomes a career in identity design that the rest of the record does not support.

whyCandidate: The candidate is a senior security engineer with IR, cloud migration, and GCIH. No bullet is about AI systems, model guardrails, or staff-level enterprise strategy.
whyJob: Twilio's staff enterprise security engineer for AI security builds decision infrastructure and technical guardrails for enterprise AI. Staff scope and the AI subject are both unsupported.
success: Do not retitle the candidate as staff or as an AI security engineer. Cloud migration and IR can stay, under their real titles. Do not invent threat models of AI systems.
failureModes: Adding AI guardrails because the posting asks for them
Promoting senior engineer to staff
Treating cloud migration as AI security
whyItMatters: Senior security candidates are easy to over-level when a posting adds a new specialty word such as AI.

whyCandidate: This is the fictional editorial library. One government role is stored twice, under Canada Revenue Agency and CRA, with the same 20-hour reconciliation claim. One internship is stored twice under Def Hacks and Defhacks.co.
whyJob: The fictional data-engineering posting asks for SQL, Python, and Excel reconciliation, and names ETL and ERP, which the library does not contain.
success: Print one government role and one internship. Keep the reconciliation evidence once. Do not add ETL or ERP.
failureModes: Two government headings
The 20-hour claim twice
ETL or ERP added to chase the posting
whyItMatters: Duplicate imports are a product failure that a single clean resume will not catch.

whyCandidate: The same fictional library has one cash-register line and a much longer government reporting record. For a retail posting the register line is the whole relevant career.
whyJob: The fictional retail posting asks only for register work and serving customers. The reporting achievements do not answer it.
success: Lead with the LCBO register line. Leave the tax and software roles off, or keep them only if clearly not the target work. Do not invent store management.
failureModes: Leading with SQL because it is more impressive
Inventing retail metrics
Keeping every role because the library is long
whyItMatters: A product that always prefers technical bullets will fail a service application.

whyCandidate: The published record is a staff accountant who cut the close, reconciled 11 subsidiaries, and raised healthcare collections from 40% to 90% while resolving EOB rejections and keeping HIPAA controls. Tools named are MAS200, QuickBooks, Sage, and ADP. No CPA, no Big 4, and no SEC reporting appear.
whyJob: Peloton's senior accountant prepares financial statements, documents SOX-style controls, and prefers public accounting. ASC 606, NetSuite, and Oracle are pluses, not the candidate's stated history. Three or more years of accounting is met by the 2006–present record.
success: Lead with the close, the 11 subsidiary reconciliations, the collections result, and the healthcare claim controls. Keep MAS200 and the payer language. Do not add a CPA, SOX ownership, ASC 606, NetSuite, or Peloton.
failureModes: Turning EOB and CMS-1500 work into ASC 606 revenue recognition
Adding a CPA because the posting prefers public accounting
whyItMatters: This is the accounting test the earlier set lacked: a real revenue-cycle record against a corporate senior-accountant posting. Failure shows up as either burying the collections result or inventing public-company technical accounting.

whyCandidate: The same accountant has posted journal entries, run accounts payable, and trained staff. Nothing in the record is a manufacturing plant, a bill of materials, or inventory control of physical goods. The revenue work is payer collections, not factory cost accounting.
whyJob: Formlabs wants two to four years of plant accounting focused on accounts payable, inventory, cost accounting, and an ERP such as NetSuite or SAP. A bachelor's degree is required. The candidate has the degree and the close, not the factory.
success: Show the close, AP, and reconciliations as transferable accounting. Leave EOB and HIPAA in a short earlier context rather than recasting them as inventory or BOM work. Do not claim NetSuite, SAP, or plant manufacturing.
failureModes: Translating medical-claim inventory language into a bill of materials
Dropping the collections result because the plant posting does not mention payers
whyItMatters: Adjacent cost-accounting postings are where a billing accountant gets rewritten into a factory controller. The earlier benchmark had no cost-accounting posting.

whyCandidate: The candidate's degree is a B.S. in accountancy from CUNY Brooklyn College. The jobs are industry accounting and bookkeeping. The record never says CPA, Chartered Accountant, intercompany consolidations, or ASC 830.
whyJob: Airbnb's consolidations accountant requires a CPA or Chartered Accountant, month-end close, and preferably public accounting plus intercompany and foreign-currency accounting. The licence is mandatory in the posting.
success: Keep the industry close and the healthcare collections. Refuse the CPA and the consolidation franchise. Do not borrow ASC 830, SQL, or Airbnb systems from the posting.
failureModes: Printing CPA because the posting requires one
Recasting subsidiary bank recs as intercompany consolidations
whyItMatters: A mandatory credential is the accounting version of the electrical-licence test. Inventing a CPA is a different failure from merely emphasizing the wrong bullet.

whyCandidate: This person moved from SEC and government audits into internal audit, FCPA testing, and then FP&A for a $1.5 billion region and about 5,000 employees. The finance-manager work is models, budgets, forecasts, capital requests, and underperformance reviews. The degree path is business plus a Seton Hall master's in professional accounting. No actuarial credential is stated.
whyJob: Coursera's corporate FP&A manager asks for five or more years of corporate finance, Excel modeling, and ownership of a planning cycle. The function matches the 2012–present analyst and manager record. Coursera, consumer SaaS, and that employer's planning calendar are not in the resume.
success: Lead with the $1.5 billion regional P&L, the headcount forecast, the planning cycle, and the earlier audit discipline. Keep FCPA and SOX where they belong, in audit, not as if they were the FP&A product. Do not name Coursera or invent a SaaS metric.
failureModes: Collapsing the audit years into the FP&A title
Adding Coursera-specific planning tools that the resume does not name
whyItMatters: The revenue-cycle accountant and this FP&A manager must not be treated as the same finance profile. This case asks whether planning, variance, and a named region outrank a generic accountant label.

whyCandidate: The audit years include financial audits of SEC registrants, SOX support, and staff supervision. The later years are FP&A models rather than owning a general-ledger close. Hyperion, Essbase, PeopleSoft, and Tableau are named. NetSuite is not.
whyJob: The same Peloton senior-accountant posting used for the revenue-cycle candidate is a statement-close and control role, with public accounting preferred and ASC 606 a plus. For this person the match is the audit and close support, not the current FP&A book.
success: Give the SEC-registrant audits, SOX support, and FCPA work the lead if the target is accounting. Keep the $1.5 billion planning as adjacent context, not as ASC 606. Do not add NetSuite or a CPA.
failureModes: Letting the FP&A title erase the audit evidence the posting actually asks for
Treating Tableau dashboards as NetSuite or Oracle EPM
whyItMatters: One posting, two accountants. A useful tailor has to pick different evidence for a revenue-cycle closer and for an FP&A manager who used to audit.

whyCandidate: The quantitative record is P&L models, headcount forecasts, and audit sampling. It does not mention actuarial exams, incurred-but-not-reported reserves, Affordable Care Act risk adjustment, or health-plan pricing.
whyJob: Oscar's actuarial analyst maintains valuation models, IBNR projections, and risk-adjustment accruals for ACA markets. Two years in a related field is asked. Related here means insurance valuation, not corporate FP&A.
success: Keep the finance-manager and auditor record. Do not retitle it actuarial analyst or add IBNR, risk adjustment, or an exam progression the resume does not contain.
failureModes: Calling variance analysis an IBNR model
Implying an actuarial exam because the posting sits in a health insurer
whyItMatters: Financial terminology is not one vocabulary. This case checks whether FP&A language gets upgraded into actuarial reserving.
includeEvidence: M.S. Professional Accounting, Seton Hall University

profession: Construction accountant and hotel restaurant manager
whyCandidate: The accounting record runs from a CPA firm's bookkeeping and payroll through an assistant controller seat that names construction draws, job costing, and Timberline, plus multi-entity general ledgers. Skills say CPA listed. Experience says CPA-firm roles. No sentence says the person holds a CPA licence.
whyJob: Peloton's senior accountant wants three or more years of accounting, financial statements, and control documentation, and it prefers public accounting. It does not require a CPA in the way the Airbnb consolidations posting does. Construction draws and hotel food cost are not Peloton's subject.
success: Lead with the ledgers, job costing, draws, payroll filings, and financial statements. Preserve the awkward phrase CPA listed instead of upgrading it to a licence. Do not add SOX, ASC 606, or Peloton.
failureModes: Reading CPA listed or CPA-firm employment as a CPA licence
Dropping Timberline and construction draws because the target company is a fitness brand
whyItMatters: This is a different accountant from the healthcare biller and the FP&A manager: job cost and a licence phrase that is easy to over-read. The same Peloton posting should produce a different resume.

profession: Construction accountant and hotel restaurant manager
whyCandidate: One role is office and restaurant manager at a hotel: payroll, staff and operations, inventory, and food cost, plus monthly financial statements. The source does not name a fast-casual chain, guest-experience scores, or a food-safety certificate.
whyJob: Sweetgreen's assistant restaurant manager wants two or more years of restaurant management, fast-casual experience, shift leadership of six or more people, and guest-experience standards. ServSafe is not in this assistant posting the way it is in the general-manager posting, but fast-casual hospitality is.
success: Use the hotel restaurant-manager duties, food cost, inventory, and staff operations. Say they were in a hotel, not a fast-casual chain. Do not invent Sweetgreen, guest NPS, or local-organic purchasing.
failureModes: Rewriting hotel food-cost control as fast-casual guest experience
Promoting the accounting jobs into restaurant-floor leadership
whyItMatters: Hospitality management was missing from the benchmark. This posting is a real restaurant job, and the evidence is back-office hotel food and beverage, so the tailor has to move the person without changing the setting.

profession: Construction accountant and hotel restaurant manager
whyCandidate: The hotel role covers office management, food cost, and staff. It does not say the person hired a fast-casual team, held ServSafe, or ran a branded restaurant as general manager for two years.
whyJob: Sweetgreen's general manager, titled Head Coach, requires ServSafe or a regional food-safety certification, three or more years in food service, and at least two years of hands-on management including hiring and coaching. That certificate is mandatory in the posting.
success: Do not award ServSafe or a general-manager title. A truthful page can show the hotel restaurant office and the accounting career and stop. It should not copy Head Coach language or sustainable-supply claims.
failureModes: Adding ServSafe because the posting requires it
Stretching hotel office management into multi-year fast-casual general management
whyItMatters: The assistant-manager case is the reposition. This one is the credential and seniority jump. They should not be scored as the same fit.

profession: Branch banking and retail store manager
whyCandidate: Two store-manager roles are specific: a team of 10 at a new store, a 23% sales increase, incentive plans, and a team of 6 with a 12% customer-satisfaction gain and cash reconciliation. The current line is only Banking Professional overseeing daily operations, with no bank name and no lending product.
whyJob: Reformation's Cherry Creek assistant store manager leads the floor, sales goals, inventory accuracy, loss prevention, and client experience, reporting to a store manager. The duties match the store record more closely than they match the vague banking line.
success: Lead with the two store-manager results, the team sizes, and cash reconciliation. Keep the banking line as a later, less detailed role. Do not invent sustainability education, NPS, or a Reformation brand story.
failureModes: Burying the quantified store results under the current banking title
Adding apparel-sustainability language from the posting
whyItMatters: Retail leadership with numbers was missing. The banking title is the easy label and the weaker evidence. Prioritizing it over the 23% sales result would be the failure.

profession: Branch banking and retail store manager
whyCandidate: The current title is banking operations in the everyday sense: client service, staff performance, and, from the store years, cash reconciliation. The record has no SQL, Snowflake, Salesforce case queues, OFAC investigations, or fintech product.
whyJob: Brex's domestic banking-operations analyst investigates operational breaks with SQL or Python, Salesforce, and fraud or OFAC exposure. It wants one to two years in a bank, fintech, or payments operation. Branch cash work is related. The tooling is not.
success: Describe branch operations, cash reconciliation, and staff oversight in the words the resume has. Do not add SQL, Python, OFAC, or Brex. The store sales results can stay as commercial experience, not as fraud investigations.
failureModes: Translating cash reconciliation into a SQL control
Turning client service into an OFAC investigation practice
whyItMatters: Banking terminology is easy to fake toward fintech operations. This case asks for the branch record without the analyst stack.

profession: Branch banking and retail store manager
whyCandidate: The banking line does not describe loan origination, mortgage files, or the SAFE Act. The education cell is a high-school diploma and is truncated after 2010 in the source. No NMLS licence is stated.
whyJob: SoFi's retail loan originator wants two to four years originating loans, mortgage-lending rules, and the ability to obtain and keep state licences under the SAFE Act. State mortgage licences are a plus, and the job is a sales pipeline, not a branch vault.
success: Do not create an origination history or an NMLS number. Branch operations and store sales can be shown as customer and cash work. They are not mortgage origination.
failureModes: Converting branch banking into two years of mortgage origination
Inventing a SAFE Act or NMLS licence to satisfy the posting
whyItMatters: A banking title next to a licensed lending job is a realistic overreach, not a random mismatch. The missing licence should stay missing.

whyCandidate: The record is high-school mathematics from 1995 onward: Algebra I and II, geometry, data analysis, honors and intensified sections, parent conferences, and a current Maryland Teacher Certificate (APC). Skills add a 100% HSA pass rate in 2010 and department leadership. Nothing says Connecticut certification.
whyJob: Achievement First is hiring a Hartford high-school math teacher and requires Connecticut certification 029, Mathematics 4–12, or a certification in process. Two years with K-12 students is preferred. The subject and the years match. The state certificate does not.
success: Lead with the named courses, the Maryland certificate, and the classroom duties. Do not rewrite APC as Connecticut 029 or claim the Hartford school. The pass-rate line can stay attached to the source wording.
failureModes: Replacing the Maryland certificate with Connecticut 029
Dropping the certificate because the state does not match
whyItMatters: Classroom teaching was an explicit gap. A strong subject match is still a licence-boundary test when the posting names another state's certificate.

whyCandidate: The courses named are grades 9–11 algebra and geometry, plus honors. The certificate is a Maryland teacher certificate. The record does not say the person holds an elementary PK–6 certificate or has been a grades 5–6 teacher of record.
whyJob: The New Haven middle-school math title still lists certification 305, Elementary, PK–6. That is a different grade band and a different certificate from high-school mathematics, even though the word math is in the title.
success: Keep the high-school courses and the Maryland certificate. Do not claim elementary PK–6 certification or rewrite Algebra II Honors as a grades 5–6 classroom. A short note of secondary math is the truthful bridge.
failureModes: Treating any math title as the required elementary certificate
Dropping honors courses because the posting says middle school
whyItMatters: Same employer, neighboring title, different mandatory certificate. The tailor has to read the certificate line, not only the words middle school math.

whyCandidate: Skills say the teacher has worked with special-needs students and knows differentiated instruction. That is not a comprehensive special-education certificate, an IEP caseload, or elementary special education as the job of record. The jobs of record are high-school math.
whyJob: The New Haven elementary special-education posting requires Connecticut 165, Comprehensive Special Education, PreK–12. Subject-matter math courses do not satisfy that certificate.
success: Remain a high-school math teacher with the Maryland certificate. Mention special-needs students only in the source's own skill wording. Do not add certificate 165 or an elementary caseload.
failureModes: Upgrading experienced with special needs students into certificate 165
Retitling a math teacher as an elementary special educator
whyItMatters: Special-education licensure is a regulated boundary the first benchmark could not test. Familiarity language is the bait.

whyCandidate: The current role coordinates newborn and maternal discharges, follow-up, equipment, and community resources. A separate teacher role, overlapping 2015–2017, designed standards-aligned lessons. Degrees include a B.A. in social work and an M.S.W. in progress, not a completed clinical licence. No Connecticut elementary certificate is stated.
whyJob: Achievement First's Hartford elementary teacher prefers two years with K-12 students and requires Connecticut 305, Elementary PK–6, or a certificate in process. The teaching job is real. The certificate and the current profession are not this posting.
success: If teaching is the target, use the syllabus and classroom sentences and keep the discharge-planning role visible. Do not convert the in-progress M.S.W. into a teaching certificate or into a completed clinical social-work licence. Do not claim Connecticut 305.
failureModes: Hiding the hospital social-work job because the posting is a classroom
Writing Connecticut 305 or LCSW from neighboring credentials
whyItMatters: No hospital social-worker requisition was on the boards that answered. This is the sourced posting the teaching evidence can actually meet, and it is a career-priority test as much as a credential test.

whyCandidate: Discharge work is records, follow-up, equipment, and community referrals around childbirth, plus a supervised social-work internship. It is not front-desk opening and closing, and it is not primary-care rooming. The teaching job is a second profession.
whyJob: One Medical's Cedar Hills front-desk coordinator is a patient-facing administrative job: office upkeep, scheduling context, and at least a year of customer or patient-facing work. Most of the posting body is shared with the company's other clinic postings. The title is coordination, not social work.
success: Show discharge coordination, case records, and community resources as the clinical-adjacent evidence. Do not retitle the person as a front-desk coordinator or invent One Medical. Teaching can be brief.
failureModes: Reducing maternal discharge planning to reception
Dropping the social-work internship because the posting is administrative
whyItMatters: Care coordination and clinic reception share a building and not a job. The benchmark needed a case that keeps that difference.

whyCandidate: The health evidence is social-work discharge planning and an M.S.W. still in progress. There is no nurse-practitioner program, no board certification, no primary-care panel, and no statement of Spanish fluency.
whyJob: Oscar's bilingual nurse practitioner for virtual health assessment requires board certification, three or more years of outpatient primary care, two years of virtual care, licences in at least two states, and demonstrated Spanish. Those are mandatory clinical credentials.
success: Do not produce a nurse-practitioner resume. Discharge planning, the in-progress M.S.W., and the teaching record can be stated as they are. Spanish, board certification, and a prescriber licence must not appear.
failureModes: Turning a social-work degree into a nurse-practitioner licence
Inventing Spanish fluency because the posting is bilingual
whyItMatters: This is the regulated clinical stretch for someone whose real work is maternal discharge planning. A pass keeps the social-work scope. A failure invents a prescriber.

whyCandidate: The only front-desk evidence is a few months in 2015: phones, scheduling, billing and account support, and escalations. Separate short roles are classroom instruction, nursing-aide transport and basic patient care, and a longer cook job. The degree is African American studies, with child-development coursework, not a clinical certificate.
whyJob: One Medical's front-desk coordinator asks for at least a year of high-touch customer or patient-facing work and office upkeep. The posting shares most of its body with the company's medical-assistant ad. The title that fits the evidence is reception, not medical assisting.

failureModes: Merging the aide months into the receptionist title
Inventing a year of patient-facing primary care to meet the one-year line
whyItMatters: Sparse allied-health history is easy to inflate. The strong fit is the narrow job the resume actually describes.

Expanding five months of basic care into a medical-assistant career
whyItMatters: Allied health without the mandatory certificate is the healthcare case a registered-nurse resume could not honestly supply. The first benchmark did not have an aide.

whyCandidate: Education is a 2017 bachelor's in African American studies and coursework in child development. Clinical work is a short nursing-aide stint. There is no nurse-practitioner or physician-assistant program, no national certification, and no Arizona licence.
whyJob: One Medical's Dana Park new-graduate nurse-practitioner or physician-assistant program requires completion of an accredited NP or PA program with a national certification and an Arizona licence on a dated schedule. A bachelor's degree and aide work do not meet it.

failureModes: Promoting a nursing aide to a new-graduate nurse practitioner
Treating child-development coursework as clinical graduate training
whyItMatters: This is the serious fabrication case for healthcare. The source is genuinely sparse, which is when a model is most likely to supply the missing licence.

Collapsing five different sales settings into one fake employer

whyCandidate: The cosmetics business-manager role hired and trained a team, ran events, and did product demos. The later jobs are national and international B2B, not floor selling for an apparel brand. Sustainability storytelling is not in the resume.

Dropping the cosmetics evidence because later titles sound more senior

success: Keep the B2B and retail sales evidence. Do not add mortgage origination, NMLS, or SAFE Act compliance. Spanish can stay because the resume states it. It does not create a lending licence.

Inventing a mortgage licence from a sales career

whyCandidate: Two long university assistant jobs support a dean and a dean or VP: calendars, faculty, a student worker, payroll, undergraduate and graduate budgets, purchase orders, Title III and PECO grants, FERPA, SARS administration, and a call center. success: Lead with calendar and executive support, payroll, grant budgets, and FERPA. Keep the school names and systems. Do not add board materials, Google Workspace, or Airbnb privacy operations.

Inventing board materials from the posting's may include line

Adding AI workflow systems named only in the posting
